Language practices can help sustain discrimination and reproduce unequal power relations by misrepresenting or describing inaccurately a certain aspect of reality. This is done by: • repeatedly using some words to describe certain groups • not having or choosing not to use certain words to describe a certain aspect of reality, such as group or issue making it invisible • loading some words negatively or positively and always using them to describe a group. These mechanisms are illustrated in the following examples: GENDER-BIASED LANGUAGE Word choices often reflect assumptions about gender roles. For example, writing “If an educator is dedicated, he will succeed” (use of generic male pro- noun) suggests it is a male who will succeed. A gender-neutral alternative would be “Educators who are dedicated will succeed” (use of “they”). Using a gender neutral “they” or “he” and “she” simultaneously or even “she” in a ge- neric form can expose the taken-for-granted use of the male pronoun. Anoth- er example of gender-biased language is using certain words to represent fe- males and males which reinforce inaccurate stereotypic gendered attributes, for example, girls are timid and boys are brave. “ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS” Often referring to immigrants or asylum seekers, the term ‘illegal immigrants’ is used in the media. Using the word “illegal” suggests there is a “wrong doing” and that the person committed a crime. European human rights commissioner Nils Muižnieks explained: “People are not illegal.
